title: Container Bookings: Destination Changes Still Awaiting Their Fee
content:
Whether a Container Bookings booking still owes a change-of-destination fee is read from its own charge history, by setting the port-of-discharge changes logged on it against the fees already booked for such changes.

## Rule

The number of destination changes still owing a fee equals the count of amendment log entries on the booking whose amendment kind is a change of port of discharge, less the count of change-of-destination fee entries on the same booking. When that number is zero, no change-of-destination fee is charged.

Every change-of-destination fee entry names, as its vessel and voyage, the sailing shown on the port-of-discharge amendment log entry it settles. That sailing is the one to which the booking was allocated at the time the change was logged, which may differ from the sailing the booking holds today.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** the booking's charge history.
- **Judgement:** count the port-of-discharge amendment log entries; count the change-of-destination fee entries; take the difference.
- **Output:** the number of changes still owing a fee, and for each, the sailing printed on its amendment log entry.

## Hypothetical cases

| Port-of-discharge log entries | Change-of-destination fee entries | Changes still owing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 |

In the second row, the fee entry to be added names the sailing on the log entry that has no fee against it. Suppose that change was logged while the booking sat on an invented sailing "AHL TAGUS 118E" and the booking has since been moved to another voyage: the new fee entry still names "AHL TAGUS 118E". The vessel names and counts are illustrative only.
